## scene

### `scene.entity(name?: string) -> entity`

create a new empty entity and return its id. With `name` it is also registered under that world name (looked up by scene.get_entity, used in URLs and spawn ref resolution). An entity does nothing until components are emplaced on it; destroy it with scene.destroy.

```lua
local e = scene.entity("hero")
```

### `scene.emplace(e: entity, type: string, fields?: table)`

create (or replace) component `type` on e from a field table; see the Component Reference below for valid types and fields. Omitted fields take their C++ defaults; an unknown type or malformed field is an error. A Geometry table may additionally carry "shapes" = an array of shape-key tables {name, pos, nrm?, uv?, idx?}. Returns nothing - read the result back with scene.component(e, type).

```lua
local e = scene.entity()
scene.emplace(e, "Transform", { pos = {0, 2, 0}, quat = {0, 0.7071, 0, 0.7071} })
```

### `scene.replace(e: entity, type: string, fields?: table)`

like scene.emplace, but the component must already exist on e (error otherwise); use it to rewrite a whole component in place. Same field-table rules as emplace (a Geometry table may carry "shapes").

### `scene.has(e: entity, type: string) -> bool`

true if e carries component `type` (a reflected component name such as "Transform" or "RigidBody"); false for unknown types.

### `scene.component(e: entity, type: string) -> table|nil`

a live view of component `type` on e (nil when absent). Reads resolve on every access, so the view always sees current values; writes go straight into the component and require it to already exist (create it with scene.emplace/replace first). The view is not a copy - do not keep it alive across scene.destroy calls. Unknown types are an error; engine-state types (e.g. "KeyboardInput") are reported as such. vec3 fields read as {x,y,z}, quats as {x,y,z,w}.

```lua
local t = scene.component(e, "Transform")
print(t.pos[1])        -- live x position
t.quat = {0, 0, 0, 1}  -- write-through (component must exist)
```

### `scene.remove(e: entity, type: string)`

remove component `type` from e; errors if the type is unknown or the component is absent. Any live views of it become invalid afterwards.

### `scene.set_pose(e: entity|string, pos: vec3, quat: quat)`

set the local Transform of e (pos = {x,y,z}, quat = {x,y,z,w}); errors if e has no Transform. Local means relative to e's parent - read the composed result with world_pose. Scale is untouched.

### `scene.get_pose(e: entity|string) -> table`

the local Transform of e as {pos = {x,y,z}, quat = {x,y,z,w}}; errors if e has no Transform. A snapshot - copy it, mutate, and write back with set_pose to animate.

```lua
local p = scene.get_pose("cube")
print(p.pos[1], p.quat[4])  -- x position, quaternion w
```

### `scene.world_pose(e: entity|string) -> table`

the world-space pose of e as {pos = {x,y,z}, quat = {x,y,z,w}}. This walks Transform+Parent live, so it is always current (unlike the per-substep WorldTransform snapshot the renderer uses). Errors if e has no Transform.

### `scene.set_morph(e: entity|string, name: string, weight: number)`

set the blend weight (0..1) of shape key `name` on mesh e; when e is a skinned character (no Geometry of its own) the weight is applied to every mesh linked to its Skeleton. List available keys with scene.shapes.

### `scene.shapes(e: entity|string) -> table`

the shape keys of mesh e as an array of {name = string, weight = number} (empty array when the mesh has none); errors if e has no Geometry.

```lua
for _, s in ipairs(scene.shapes("cube")) do print(s.name, s.weight) end
```

### `scene.link_mesh(skel: entity|string, mesh: entity|string)`

add mesh to the skinned-mesh list of skeleton skel so it is posed by the same bones and receives scene.set_morph weights; errors if skel has no Skeleton.

### `scene.spawn(tbl: table, parent?: entity|string) -> table`

materialize a name->node map into live entities in one call. Each node is a component-name -> field-table map (e.g. {Transform = {...}, RigidBody = {...}}); the map key becomes the world name (suffixed "#2", "#3", ... when the name is already taken), and "Name" keys inside a node are ignored. Refs: an integer is used as-is; a string resolves against this spawn's names first, then world names. A Renderable without "geom" defaults to the node's own Geometry. `parent` (entity or name, must have a Transform) parents every root node that has no Parent of its own. Returns the name->entity map.

```lua
local e = scene.spawn({
    col  = { CapsuleShape = { halfLen = 0.5, radius = 0.3 } },
    body = { Transform = { pos = {0, 1, 0} },
             RigidBody = { mass = 10, colliders = { "col" } } },
})
print(e.body)  -- the rigid-body entity
```

### `scene.get_entity(name: string) -> entity|nil`

look up a world name (as given to scene.entity or produced by scene.spawn); nil when no such entity exists.

### `scene.get_script(target: string|entity) -> table|nil`

the instance table of the script attached to the named entity (or the given entity) - the same table its hooks receive as self, so per-instance fields are readable and writable and module functions act as methods (`other:fn()`). nil when no ready script is attached. Don't hold it across destroys or re-attaches; fetch fresh each use.

### `scene.name(e: entity) -> string|nil`

the world name of e (as given to scene.entity or produced by scene.spawn); nil when e has no Name component. The reverse of get_entity.

### `scene.named() -> table`

every named entity as an array of {name = string, entity = entity}, sorted by entity id (the scene editor's source list).

### `scene.components(e: entity) -> table`

the reflected component type names on e as an array of strings (e.g. {"Transform", "RigidBody"}); the scene editor's field-list source.

### `scene.find_components(component: string, root?: entity) -> table`

every entity carrying `component` in root's subtree (root included) as an array of entities; when root is omitted, all top-level entities are searched - i.e. the whole world.

### `scene.attach_script(e: entity, file: string, params?: table) -> table|nil`

attach a Lua module to e and activate it immediately, returning its instance table (the same table its hooks receive as self; nil when the module fails to load, error printed). Re-attaching replaces any existing script on e. `file` is resolved against the scenes dir ("scenes/camera" or "camera.lua"); the module must return a table whose hooks (_on_ready, _animate, _physics - see Script Hooks below) are called with the instance table as self. `params` is passed to _on_ready. Top-level variables in the module are exposed as "name.LuaScript.<var>" URLs (bindable by UI widgets).

```lua
local cam = scene.entity("cam")
local fly = scene.attach_script(cam, "scenes/camera")  -- fly camera: look + wasd/qe movement
```

### `scene.destroy(e: entity)`

destroy e and its whole subtree (all components, world names released). Errors when e is a shape still referenced by a collider, a texture referenced by a material, or a geometry referenced by a renderable outside the subtree - remove those references first. A no-op for already-destroyed entities.

### `scene.add_child(parent: entity, child: entity, opts?: table)`

reparent child under parent (parent needs a Transform; replaces any existing Parent on child). With opts.keepWorld = true the child's local pose is re-expressed first so its world position does not change.

### `scene.set(target: entity|string, field: string, value: number|table|string)`

set a reflected field. Two forms: (entity, "field", value) writes one component field on an entity, or ("Name.Component.field", value) walks a URL to a scalar/vec3/quat/color field; ("name.LuaScript.var", string) sets a script variable. `value` is a number, an array of up to 4 numbers (pos/quat/color), or a string for LuaScript targets. Errors on unknown names or fields.

### `scene.get(target: entity|string, field?: string) -> number|vec3|vec4|string`

read a reflected field. (entity, "field") reads one component field; ("Name.Component.field") walks a URL; ("name.LuaScript.var") reads a script variable as a string. Returns a scalar for 1-component fields, {x,y,z} for vec3/color, {x,y,z,w} for quats, or the string itself for LuaScript targets. Errors on unknown names or fields.

### `scene.time() -> number`

seconds since engine start (monotonic); use it for _animate timing rather than accumulating dt yourself.

### `scene.fields(type: string) -> table`

the reflected field metadata of component type as an array of {name = string, kind = string, lo = number, hi = number}; kind is one of slider_f, slider_i, checkbox, color, drag_v3, ref, str, str_arr, quat, float_arr, uint_arr, ent_arr. Empty table for unknown types.

### `scene.scenes() -> table`

the loadable scenes in the active scenes dir as an array of {label = string, path = string}; label comes from the json "name" field when present, else the file stem. Feed `path` to request_scene.

### `scene.request_scene(path: string)`

queue a scene (a `path` from scene.scenes()) to load at the end of this frame - the usual way for a UI button to switch scenes. Check scene.last_error() afterwards if it fails.

### `scene.last_error() -> string`

the error message from the last failed scene load, or "" when the last load succeeded (or none was attempted).

### `scene.animate(target, field, keys, opts?) -> entity`

keyframe animation built from a generated clip + player. target = named entity, name string, or an array of them (one track per target, shared clock); field = "Component.field"; keys = array of {t = seconds, v = number|{n1..n4}} sorted by t (all keys must carry the same value count 1/3/4); opts = {loop = 0 once, 1 loop (default), 2 pingpong; speed = number (default 1); playing = bool (default true)}. Returns the AnimationPlayer entity - control it with scene.component(player, "AnimationPlayer") or destroy it to stop.

```lua
local p = scene.animate("cube", "Transform.pos", {
    { t = 0, v = {0, 0, 0} }, { t = 1, v = {2, 0, 0} }, { t = 2, v = {0, 0, 0} },
}, { loop = 1 })
```

## math

_Vector/quaternion helpers added on top of Lua's standard `math` library_

### `math.vadd(a: vec3, b: vec3) -> vec3`

element-wise vector addition (vec3 = {x,y,z})

### `math.vsub(a: vec3, b: vec3) -> vec3`

element-wise vector subtraction

### `math.vscale(v: vec3, s: number) -> vec3`

scalar multiplication (each component * s)

### `math.vlen(v: vec3) -> number`

Euclidean length of v (0 for the zero vector)

### `math.vnorm(v: vec3) -> vec3`

unit-length (normalized) copy of v; undefined for the zero vector

### `math.vcross(a: vec3, b: vec3) -> vec3`

cross product a x b (perpendicular to both; zero when parallel)

### `math.vdot(a: vec3, b: vec3) -> number`

dot product a . b (|a||b|cos of the angle between them)

### `math.qmul(a: quat, b: quat) -> quat`

quaternion product a * b (quat = {x,y,z,w}); applying the result to a vector rotates by b first, then a - so qmul(delta, current) prepends delta to current

### `math.qinv(q: quat) -> quat`

inverse (conjugate) of q; qmul(q, qinv(q)) is the identity rotation

### `math.qaxis(axis: vec3, angle: number) -> quat`

axis-angle to quaternion (angle in radians; the axis is normalized internally)

### `math.qrot(q: quat, v: vec3) -> vec3`

rotate vector v by quaternion q

### `math.qfromto(a: vec3, b: vec3) -> quat`

the shortest rotation mapping direction a onto b (both normalized internally); handy for aiming one object at another

## graphics

### `graphics.gltf(path: string) -> table`

parse a glTF file as a name->node map (node = component-name -> field table) without creating world entities - pass the result to scene.spawn to materialize it. Nodes carry Transform, Parent, Geometry, Renderable, Material, Skeleton, AnimationClip and AnimationPlayer components; refs inside are strings that scene.spawn resolves. Compat form: graphics.gltf(e, path) loads straight into entity e and returns e.

### `graphics.load_texture(path: string, name?: string) -> entity`

create a Texture entity holding `path` (the file is loaded and uploaded to the GPU lazily on first use); optionally register it under `name`. Use as Material.tex/texMR/ texNormal/texEmissive.

### `graphics.render_texture(w: int, h: int, name?: string) -> entity`

create a standalone GPUTexture render target of w x h pixels (no Texture parent); render into it, then attach it to a material or environment. Errors when the graphics server is disabled.

## physics

### `physics.fit_capsule(pos: number[], nrm?: number[], opts?: table) -> table, err`

fit a compound of tapered-capsule chains (spheres for blob-like clouds) to a vertex cloud. `pos` is flat xyz (at least 3 vertices); `nrm` is flat xyz outward normals of the same length (positions-only fit when absent). `opts` overrides profile_bins, profile_percentile, profile_dilate, underfit_weight, overfit_weight, tolerance, max_segments, overhang_weight, overhang_percentile, sphere_aspect, sphere_percentile, max_clusters. Returns nil + message when nothing fits. Result: {ok = true, underfit = number, overhang = number, score = number, parts = array of part}, where part = {origin = vec3, axis = vec3 (unit), length = number, segments = int, rms_error, max_error, mean_signed_error, profile_score, overhang_score, tapers = array of {s0, s1, r0, r1}}; a part with length 0 and one taper r0 = r1 is a sphere. Feed the parts straight into TaperedCapsule components (one entity per part).

```lua
local fit, err = physics.fit_capsule(pos, nrm)
if not fit then error(err) end
for _, p in ipairs(fit.parts) do print(p.length, p.rms_error) end
```

### `physics.raycast(origin: vec3, dir: vec3, maxDist: number, excludes?: table) -> table|nil`

rigid-body raycast against the Jolt world. Returns {hit = true, pos = {x,y,z}, dist = number, entity = entity} (entity omitted when the hit body has no owning entity), or nil when nothing is hit within maxDist. `excludes` is an array of entities whose colliders are skipped.

```lua
local h = physics.raycast({0, 5, 0}, {0, -1, 0}, 10)
if h then print("floor at", h.pos[2]) end
```

### `physics.convex_decompose(mesh: entity|table, maxHulls?: number, maxVertsPerHull?: number, threshold?: number) -> table`

decompose a mesh into convex hulls (CoACD). `mesh` is an entity with Geometry or a raw Geometry field table {pos, nrm?, uv?, idx}. Returns an array of hulls, each a flat {x,y,z,...} point list ready for ConvexHullShape.points; falls back to one hull of all vertices on degenerate input.

### `physics.collision_exception(a: entity, b: entity, on?: bool)`

toggle the collision exclusion between two rigid bodies: on = true (default) makes them ignore each other, false restores normal collision; effective from the next physics step. Typical use: exclude a character's own colliders or jointed parts from each other.

## soft

### `soft.set_floor(y: number)`

set the Y height of the cloth/soft-body floor plane; errors when the graphics server is disabled.

### `soft.set_pins(e: entity, weights: table)`

per-vertex pin weights for a soft body: one number in [0,1] per vertex (0 = free, 1 = hard pin). Pinned vertices are pulled toward their pin targets with step-independent stiffness. Targets track the body's own node transform every frame (rest pose x its live world transform), so moving the cloth's Transform — or any ancestor — drags the pins with it; no per-frame calls needed. An explicit pin source (soft.set_pin_source) overrides the anchor. An empty array clears all pins. Errors when e is not a soft body or the array length differs from the vertex count.

```lua
local w = {}
for i = 1, 64 * 64 do w[i] = 0 end
for i = 1, 64 do w[i] = 1 end -- pin the top row of a 64x64 cloth
soft.set_pins(cloth, w)
```

### `soft.set_pin_source(e: entity, src: entity|nil)`

set the pin-target anchor of a soft body: another mesh entity (skinned or static — its GPU vertices transformed by its node's live world transform become the targets), or nil to anchor to the body's own node (rest pose x its live world transform). Tracked every frame, so a moving anchor drags the pins with it. Takes effect immediately on the next step.

```lua
soft.set_pin_source(cloth, characterMesh)
```

### `soft.set_pin_map(e: entity, map: table|nil)`

remap pin targets when the cloth and anchor mesh have different topology: one number per cloth vertex — vertex i takes its target from source vertex map[i]. nil (or an empty array) restores the identity mapping. Takes effect immediately on the next step.

### `soft.update_pins(e: entity)`

kept for compatibility; a no-op now that pin targets track their anchor's live world transform every frame (moving anchors drag the pins automatically).

## ui

### `ui.seq() -> number`

the next UI layout order number. Call it once per widget you create and store it in the widget's "order" field (the `ui` stdlib does this for you); the counter is shared with the C++ spawn functions so layout stays stable across frames.

### `ui.fire_button(url: string)`

call the function named by a "name.LuaScript.fn" URL with no argument - the headless stand-in for a button click or widget change (used by tests).

## engine

### `engine.performance_metrics() -> string`

the engine's per-frame performance summary (fps + per-phase ms averages), refreshed by the engine every frame; poll it from _animate to display in a UI text widget.

## input

### `input.key_down(kb: entity, code: number) -> bool`

true while key `code` (a GLFW key code, e.g. 65 = 'A', 32 = space) is held on the KeyboardInput entity kb; false for out-of-range codes or when kb has no KeyboardInput. Find the entity with scene.find_components("KeyboardInput").

## components (emplace / replace)

_Emplaced via `scene.emplace(e, "Type", {fields})`, replaced via `scene.replace(...)`; all fields are optional (defaults come from the C++ struct). Entity refs accept an entity or a named-entity string._

### Transform

position/scale/rotation of an entity; `quat` is {x,y,z,w} and may also be written via qx..qw

| field | type | range | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| pos | vec3 |  | local position relative to the parent (meters); set via scene.set_pose or drag in the editor |
| scale | vec3 |  | local scale multiplier per axis (1 = unchanged) |
| quat | quat |  | local rotation {x,y,z,w} (w last; identity = {0,0,0,1}) |
| qx | number | [-1.0, 1.0] | slider alias for quat.x |
| qy | number | [-1.0, 1.0] | slider alias for quat.y |
| qz | number | [-1.0, 1.0] | slider alias for quat.z |
| qw | number | [-1.0, 1.0] | slider alias for quat.w |

### Bind

per-frame URL copy: source `url` -> `target` field (empty = widget value); `dir` 0=Both 1=Read 2=Write

| field | type | range | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| url | string |  | source URL ("Name.Component.field" or "name.LuaScript.var") |
| target | string |  | destination field of this entity (empty = the widget's own value) |
| dir | int | [0.0, 2.0] | 0 = Both, 1 = Read (display only), 2 = Write (write-back only) |

### AnimationClip

keyframe clip asset: duration + per-track target URLs and flat keyframe arrays (times/values concatenated; tangents for cubic). glTF clips are populated eagerly by loadGltf/gltfToData.

| field | type | range | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| duration | number | [0.0, 3600.0] | clip length in seconds (auto-derived from the last keyframe when 0) |
| targets | string[] |  | one target URL per track ("Name.Component.field") |
| interps | number[] |  | per-track interpolation: 0 = linear, 1 = step, 2 = cubic |
| trackStart | number[] |  | track i owns keyframes [trackStart[i], trackStart[i+1]) (n+1 entries, last = total) |
| times | number[] |  | keyframe times, concatenated per track (sorted within a track) |
| values | number[] |  | keyframe values, concatenated per track (field width x key count per track) |
| tangents | number[] |  | optional cubic tangents: 2*(n-1)*width floats per track, [outT0, inT1, outT1, ...] |

### AnimationPlayer

plays an AnimationClip: `clip` = clip entity ref, time/speed, loop 0=once 1=loop 2=pingpong, playing start/stop

| field | type | range | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| clip | entity-ref |  | the AnimationClip entity to play |
| time | number | [0.0, 3600.0] | playback time in seconds (advanced by dt*speed while playing) |
| speed | number | [-4.0, 4.0] | playback rate (negative = reverse) |
| loop | int | [0.0, 2.0] | 0 = once (clamped), 1 = loop, 2 = pingpong |
| playing | bool |  | pause/resume playback |

### UIWidget

marker for a drawable UI widget; `order` is its layout position among siblings

| field | type | range | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| order | int | [0.0, 10000.0] | layout position among siblings (call ui.seq() when creating by hand) |

### UIButton

a clickable button; on click the exported function named by `target_url` is called with this entity as arg 1

| field | type | range | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| label | string |  | button text |
| target_url | string |  | "name.LuaScript.fn" called on click (this entity as arg 1) |

### UICanvas

a UI canvas: its own GPU texture + quad; `w`/`h` are the full size in meters

| field | type | range | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| w | number |  | canvas width in world meters (pixels * 0.0022) |
| h | number |  | canvas height in world meters |

### GPUTexture

an allocated GPU texture (pixel size); created for canvas entities

| field | type | range | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| w | int | [0.0, 16384.0] | width in pixels |
| h | int | [0.0, 16384.0] | height in pixels |

### UIWindow

an ImGui window filling its canvas; `pos` comes from the canvas Transform (set it explicitly)

| field | type | range | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| title | string |  | window title bar text |
| canvas | entity-ref |  | the UICanvas entity this window is drawn on |
| w | number |  | window width in pixels (the canvas Transform places it) |
| h | number |  | window height in pixels |
| flags | int | [0.0, 1000000.0] | ImGui window flags (e.g. 294 = no move/collapse/resize/settings) |
| order | int | [0.0, 10000.0] | layout order among windows on the same canvas |

### UITab

a tab page inside a UI window

| field | type | range | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| label | string |  | tab label; widgets parented under it draw on this page |

### UIText

a static (or bound) text line

| field | type | range | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| label | string |  | the text to show (live-updates when bound via Bind) |

### UISection

a (collapsible by default) labeled section; its children are added to it

| field | type | range | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| label | string |  | section header text |
| collapsible | bool |  | collapse/expand the section |

### UISliderF

a float slider; `change_url` is called with this entity as arg 1 while the user drags it

| field | type | range | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| label | string |  | slider label |
| value | number |  | current value (bound live via Bind when present) |
| lo | number |  | minimum |
| hi | number |  | maximum |
| fmt | string |  | printf format for the readout (e.g. "%.2f") |
| change_url | string |  | "name.LuaScript.fn" called while the user drags (this entity as arg 1) |

### UISliderI

an integer slider; `change_url` is called with this entity as arg 1 while the user drags it

| field | type | range | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| label | string |  | slider label |
| value | int |  | current value (bound live via Bind when present) |
| lo | int |  | minimum |
| hi | int |  | maximum |
| change_url | string |  | "name.LuaScript.fn" called while the user drags (this entity as arg 1) |

### UICheckbox

a bool checkbox; `change_url` is called with this entity as arg 1 when toggled

| field | type | range | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| label | string |  | checkbox label |
| value | bool |  | checked state (bound live via Bind when present) |
| change_url | string |  | "name.LuaScript.fn" called when toggled (this entity as arg 1) |

### UIColorEdit

an RGB (0..1) color picker; `change_url` is called with this entity as arg 1 while the user edits it

| field | type | range | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| label | string |  | picker label |
| value | vec3 |  | current color {r,g,b} (bound live via Bind when present) |
| change_url | string |  | "name.LuaScript.fn" called while the user edits (this entity as arg 1) |

### UIDragV3

a 3D drag gizmo; `change_url` is called with this entity as arg 1 while the user drags it

| field | type | range | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| label | string |  | gizmo label |
| value | vec3 |  | current value {x,y,z} (bound live via Bind when present) |
| speed | number |  | drag sensitivity (units per pixel) |
| change_url | string |  | "name.LuaScript.fn" called while the user drags (this entity as arg 1) |

### Material

PBR material: baseColor/emissive (vec3), metallic/roughness [0,1], up to 4 texture refs (tex/texMR/texNormal/texEmissive), alphaMode 0=opaque 1=mask 2=blend, SSS and refraction

| field | type | range | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| baseColor | vec3 |  | albedo RGB (0..1); multiplied with tex when present |
| metallic | number | [0.0, 1.0] | metalness 0..1 (1 = pure metal, no diffuse lobe) |
| roughness | number | [0.0, 1.0] | surface roughness 0..1 (0 = mirror-like) |
| emissive | vec3 |  | unlit HDR emission added to the color; multiplied by texEmissive when present |
| tex | entity-ref |  | base-color texture entity (Texture or GPUTexture) |
| texMR | entity-ref |  | glTF metallicRoughness texture (G = roughness, B = metallic) |
| texNormal | entity-ref |  | normal map; strength scaled by normalScale |
| texEmissive | entity-ref |  | emissive texture (multiplied with emissive) |
| alphaMode | int | [0.0, 2.0] | 0 = opaque, 1 = mask (discard where alpha < alphaCutoff), 2 = blend |
| alphaCutoff | number | [0.0, 1.0] | discard threshold in mask mode |
| alpha | number | [0.0, 1.0] | constant opacity multiplier (mask/blend) |
| ssssWeight | vec3 |  | per-channel subsurface-scatter blur distance (R/G/B); 0 = off; scaled by ssssScale |
| refraction | number | [-1.0, 1.0] | glass amount 0..1 (>0 samples the scene color through Snell's law at ior) |
| ior | number | [1.0, 1.8] | index of refraction for the glass bend (1.5 ~ glass) |
| normalScale | number | [0.0, 3.0] | normal-map strength multiplier |
| ssssScale | number | [0.0, 1.0] | overall SSS blur-distance scale |
| ssssSplit | number | [0.0, 1.0] | fraction of the albedo routed to the blurred (pre-scatter) half, 0..1 |

### MaterialRef

points an entity at the Material entity used for its rendering (`material` = material entity)

| field | type | range | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| material | entity-ref |  | the Material entity this entity renders with |

### Parent

scene hierarchy: `e` = parent entity

| field | type | range | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| e | entity-ref |  | the parent entity; the local Transform is relative to it |

### Camera

camera: fovDeg/nearP/farP; `active=true` makes it THE camera (first active wins); XR hand-off deactivates all non-VR cameras while the headset has a pose

| field | type | range | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| fovDeg | number | [10.0, 120.0] | vertical field of view in degrees |
| nearP | number | [0.01, 5.0] | near clip plane (meters) |
| farP | number | [10.0, 1000.0] | far clip plane (meters) |
| active | bool |  | true makes this THE camera (first active wins); XR hand-off deactivates non-VR cameras |

### Environment

environment lighting: intensity + environment texture ref (`tex`)

| field | type | range | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| intensity | number | [0.0, 10.0] | environment-light multiplier |
| tex | entity-ref |  | HDRI texture entity for image-based lighting and reflections |

### PointLight

point light: color (vec3), intensity, radius (falloff), on 0/1, shadow tuning fields

| field | type | range | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| on | number | [0.0, 1.0] | 0/1 switch |
| color | vec3 |  | RGB tint of the light |
| intensity | number | [0.0, 1000.0] | radiometric power (higher = brighter) |
| radius | number | [0.0, 2.0] | sphere-light physical radius (meters): sets specular/penumbra softness; falloff is inverse-square |
| shadowNear | number | [0.001, 1.0] | shadow-map near clip (meters) |
| shadowFar | number | [1.0, 100.0] | shadow-map far clip (meters) |
| shadowNormalBias | number | [0.0, 1.0] | shadow acne tuning: push samples along the normal |
| shadowBiasBase | number | [0.0, 2.0] | shadow acne tuning: constant depth bias |
| shadowBiasSlope | number | [0.0, 4.0] | shadow acne tuning: slope-scaled depth bias |
| shadowSearchScale | number | [0.5, 16.0] | contact-hardening search scale (higher = tighter penumbra) |
| shadowMaxRadius | number | [1.0, 64.0] | maximum penumbra radius in the shadow map |

### SoftBodyData

GPU PBD soft-body params: pinned (0=free, >0=pinned), solver steps/passes, mass/damping/stiffness/tension/friction, cons = constraint param array, per-vertex pinning (pinW/pinMap/pinSrc)

| field | type | range | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| pinned | int | [0.0, 2.0] | 0 = free, >0 = held in place (e.g. a fixed cloth anchor) |
| steps | int | [1.0, 32.0] | substeps per frame (dt is divided by this; damping is applied per substep) |
| mass | number | [0.1, 10.0] | body mass (kg) |
| damping | number | [0.9, 1.0] | velocity retention per frame (1 = no damping; applied as a per-substep factor) |
| passes | int | [1.0, 16.0] | PBD constraint-solver iterations per substep |
| stiffness | number | [0.0, 1.0] | constraint stiffness (higher = less compliant; alpha = 10/stiff) |
| tension | number | [0.5, 1.5] | global rest-length scale for all constraints (1 = as built; >1 stretches the cloth) |
| friction | number | [0.0, 50.0] | contact friction: caps tangential slip per contact correction |
| cons | number[] |  | distance constraints as flat {a, b, rest, k} quads (vertex indices, rest length, stiffness) |
| pinW | number[] |  | per-vertex pin weight in [0,1], one entry per vertex (0 = free); pulls the vertex toward its pin target with step-independent stiffness (1 = hard pin) |
| pinMap | int[] |  | optional target remap: cloth vertex i takes its pin target from source vertex pinMap[i] (default identity) |
| pinSrc | entity-ref |  | pin target source mesh entity (null = the body's own current positions); refreshed by soft.update_pins |

### RigidBody

Jolt dynamic body: friction/restitution/damping/mass, forceSleep, `colliders` = collider entities

| field | type | range | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| friction | number | [0.0, 1.0] | Coulomb friction coefficient 0..1 |
| restitution | number | [0.0, 1.0] | bounciness 0..1 (1 = perfectly elastic) |
| damping | number | [0.0, 1.0] | linear velocity damping 0..1 |
| mass | number | [0.0, 1000.0] | mass in kg (0 = static body) |
| forceSleep | bool |  | force the body to sleep immediately |
| colliders | entity[] |  | collider entities attached to this body |
| force | vec3 |  | persistent external force (N), applied every physics step until changed |
| impulse | vec3 |  | one-shot impulse (N*s), applied on the next step then cleared to zero |

### KinematicBody

Jolt kinematic (script-driven) body: `colliders` = collider entities

| field | type | range | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| colliders | entity[] |  | collider entities attached to this body; move it by writing its Transform |

### SixDofJoint

6-DOF joint: bodyA/bodyB refs (null bodyB = fixed to world), translation/angle limits (lim*), soft limits, per-axis motors (motor*), priority/solver steps, enabled

| field | type | range | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| bodyA | entity-ref |  | first body entity |
| bodyB | entity-ref |  | second body entity (null = fixed to the world) |
| grabPos | vec3 |  | world-space point grabbed when the joint is created |
| worldSpace | bool |  | interpret limits/motors in world space instead of body A's frame |
| relQuat | quat |  | relative orientation locked between the two bodies {x,y,z,w} |
| axisQuat | quat |  | joint-axis frame rotation {x,y,z,w} (limits/motors are expressed in it) |
| limOn | bool |  | enable the translation/angle limits below |
| limTransMin | vec3 |  | min translation limit {x,y,z} (meters; use +/-1e30 to lock an axis) |
| limTransMax | vec3 |  | max translation limit {x,y,z} (meters) |
| limAngMin | vec3 |  | min swing/twist angle limits {x,y,z} (radians) |
| limAngMax | vec3 |  | max swing/twist angle limits {x,y,z} (radians; 0 = locked) |
| softTransFreq | vec3 |  | soft-limit spring frequency per axis (Hz; 0 = hard limit) |
| softTransDamp | vec3 |  | soft-limit spring damping per axis |
| pyramid | bool |  | swing constraint shape: true = pyramid (box-like), false = cone |
| frictionTrans | vec3 |  | idle friction per axis (translation) |
| frictionAng | vec3 |  | idle friction per axis (rotation) |
| motorState | number[] |  | motor state per axis: 0 = off, 1 = velocity, 2 = position |
| motorMode | number[] |  | motor spring mode per axis: 0 = off, 1 = stiff, 2 = soft |
| motorFreq | vec3 |  | motor spring frequency per axis (Hz) |
| motorDamp | vec3 |  | motor spring damping per axis |
| motorForceMin | vec3 |  | min motor force per axis (N) |
| motorForceMax | vec3 |  | max motor force per axis (N) |
| motorTorqueMin | vec3 |  | min motor torque per axis (N*m) |
| motorTorqueMax | vec3 |  | max motor torque per axis (N*m) |
| motorTargetPos | vec3 |  | position-motor target offset {x,y,z} (meters) |
| motorTargetVel | vec3 |  | velocity-motor target linear velocity {x,y,z} (m/s) |
| motorTargetAngVel | vec3 |  | velocity-motor target angular velocity {x,y,z} (rad/s) |
| motorTargetQuat | quat |  | position-motor target orientation {x,y,z,w} |
| priority | int | [0.0, 1023.0] | solver priority (higher = solved first) |
| velSteps | int | [0.0, 64.0] | velocity solver iterations for this joint |
| posSteps | int | [0.0, 64.0] | position solver iterations for this joint |
| enabled | bool |  | enable/disable the joint without removing it |
| excludeCollision | bool |  | suppress collision between bodyA and bodyB |

| sssCurvScale | number | [0.0, 10.0] | SSS pass: curvature scale for the scatter kernel |
| renderScale | number | [0.25, 2.0] | scene buffer size vs display (1 = native; >1 supersamples) |

| field | type | range | description |

| positionSteps | int | [1.0, 512.0] | Jolt position solver iterations per step |

## script hooks (attached modules)

_A `.lua` file attached via `scene.attach_script(e, file, params)` must return a table (the module). The engine calls its hooks with a per-attach instance table as `self`._

### `inst` — per-attach instance table passed as self to every hook; fields: entity (the attached entity), params (the table passed to scene.attach_script, when given); its __index metatable is the module, so module functions act as methods and inst fields hold per-instance state

### `_on_ready(inst)`

called once when the attached module has loaded

### `_animate(inst, dt)`

called every frame with the frame delta time in seconds

### `_physics(inst, dt)`

called every physics tick (fixed rate, default 60 Hz, --phys-hz) before the Jolt step, with the tick dt; the place to write kinematic poses
